title: Surjectivity of first Koszul homology base change for a flat quotient
statement:
Let $A\to B$ and $A\to A'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Let $r\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in B$, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, and suppose that $B/I$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ with its tensor-product algebra multiplication, and $f_i'=f_i\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For the Koszul complexes and homology of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], the canonical $B'$-linear map
$$H_1(K_B(f_1,\ldots,f_r))\otimes_A A'\longrightarrow H_1(K_{B'}(f_1',\ldots,f_r'))$$
is surjective. On pure tensors it sends $[\sum_i b_i e_i]\otimes a'$ to the homology class of $\sum_i(b_i\otimes a')e_i$, where $\sum_i b_if_i=0$. No flatness of $B$ or $A'$ over $A$, finite-presentation, Noetherian, nonzero-ring, or nonempty-sequence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular), including the canonical map described by scalar extension of cycles.

proof.text: Put $E=B^{\oplus r}$, $F=\bigwedge_B^2E$, $Z=\ker(d_1:E\to B)$ and $H=H_1(K_B(f))$. The formulas and homology definition in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] give $d_1(e_i)=f_i$, $d_2(e_i\wedge e_j)=f_ie_j-f_je_i$, $\operatorname{im}d_1=I$, and $H=Z/\operatorname{im}d_2$. Consequently the sequences $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}B\to B/I\to0$, $Z\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{q}I\to0$, and $F\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{p}H\to0$ are exact, where $j,u$ are inclusions, $q(e_i)=f_i$, and $v$ is $d_2$ with codomain restricted to $Z$. Indeed $\ker q=Z$, $q$ is onto by generation of $I$, and $\ker p=\operatorname{im}v$ by the quotient definition.

source.place: Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular), opening complex and its three exact sequences

proof.text: Write $K'_\bullet=K_{B'}(f')$. For $n=0,1,2$, the basis $e_J$ of $K_n$ stated in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] gives an isomorphism $\alpha_n:K_n\otimes_A A'\to K'_n$ sending $(b e_J)\otimes a'$ to $(b\otimes a')e'_J$. The inverse sends $c e'_J$, for $c=\sum_t b_t\otimes a'_t\in B'$, to $\sum_t(b_t e_J)\otimes a'_t$. This is independent of the tensor expression for $c$ by the bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the two composites fix pure tensors and basis coefficients, hence are identities. The formulas for $d_1,d_2$ in step 1 show on $e_i\otimes a'$ and $(e_i\wedge e_j)\otimes a'$ that $\alpha_{n-1}(d_n\otimes1)=d'_n\alpha_n$ for $n=1,2$: both sides are respectively $(f_i\otimes a')$ and $(f_i\otimes a')e'_j-(f_j\otimes a')e'_i$. Thus the maps used below have exactly the base-changed Koszul differentials.

source.place: Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular), identification of the tensorized complex in degrees 0, 1, 2

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to I\xrightarrow{j}B\to B/I\to0$ over $A$, with $N=A'$. Its only flatness hypothesis is the assumed flatness of $B/I$. It gives injectivity of $j\otimes1:I\otimes_A A'\to B'$; to use the stated left-tensor version, conjugate by the mutually inverse flips $x\otimes a'\mapsto a'\otimes x$, which exist by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $Z\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{q}I\to0$ gives $\ker(q\otimes1)=\operatorname{im}(u\otimes1)$. Since $d'_1\alpha_1=(j\otimes1)(q\otimes1)$ and $j\otimes1$ is injective, $\alpha_1$ maps this kernel onto $Z'=\ker d'_1$. Therefore the map $t:Z\otimes_A A'\to Z'$, induced by $\alpha_1(u\otimes1)$, is surjective.

source.place: Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular), first two tensorized exact sequences and surjectivity onto the new cycle module

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $F\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{p}H\to0$, the map $p\otimes1:Z\otimes_A A'\to H\otimes_A A'$ is onto and its kernel is $\operatorname{im}(v\otimes1)$. Let $\pi':Z'\to H_1(K'_\bullet)$ be the quotient map. The map $\pi't$ annihilates $\operatorname{im}(v\otimes1)$: step 2 identifies $t(v\otimes1)$ with the second Koszul differential $d'_2\alpha_2$, whose image is a boundary. Hence it factors uniquely through a map $\beta:H\otimes_A A'\to H_1(K'_\bullet)$. It is surjective: any target homology class has a cycle representative $z'$, step 3 supplies $y\in Z\otimes_A A'$ with $t(y)=z'$, and $\beta((p\otimes1)y)=[z']$.

source.place: Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular), last tensorized exact sequence and displayed cokernel surjection

proof.text: For $z=\sum_i b_i e_i\in Z$, the construction gives $\beta([z]\otimes a')=[\sum_i(b_i\otimes a')e'_i]$, the claimed canonical map. It is $B'$-linear: for $b\in B$ and $a',c'\in A'$, multiplication by $b\otimes c'$ in the source sends $[z]\otimes a'$ to $[bz]\otimes c'a'$, and the displayed formula sends this to $(b\otimes c')\beta([z]\otimes a')$. Pure tensors generate both $B'$ and $H\otimes_A A'$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so this equality proves linearity for all scalars and elements. The argument also applies to $r=0$ (then $Z=H=0$), to zero rings, and to empty degree-two bases; it uses no flatness of $B$ or $A'$.
